fullPassage:
My Octopus Teacher

I returned to the Cape of Good Hope, South Africa, where I had spent my childhood, after over 20 years of movie-making. I went diving in the cold sea off the coast of the Cape, and it was among the dense seaweed forests where I met an octopus.

First Encounter

I saw a fish peacefully swimming near a heap of shells. Suddenly, an octopus sprang from the heap and grabbed the fish. Amazed at the cleverness of the octopus, I swam a little closer, but it disappeared. In fact, it had lifted a piece of seaweed, wrapped it around itself, and was staring at me out of a little gap. What an extraordinary creature! I wondered what would happen if I kept watching it. To see the world from the octopus's perspective, I left a camera near the den and started visiting regularly. I even mapped the environment around the den. Expecting some drama to come, I waited.

Making Friends

The octopus became less scared as I visited more often. After about a month, it came near me. I put my hand out, and it reached out to me. After another week, it started to wave like a human friend saying, "Hi, I'm excited to see you." I kept still, and it covered my whole hand. Since I had to take a breath, I swam toward the surface. To my surprise, it rode on my hand all the way to the top. There I was, just staring into the eyes of this incredible creature. It sparked my curiosity in a way that I had not experienced before. Had I gained its trust? I started reading books about octopuses, but I wanted to learn more about this marvelous creature. The first thing I learned was that "it" was a "she."

Getting Closer

Danger in the form of pyjama sharks, the area's biggest predators, came with little warning in the sea. The octopus was moving around near the edge of the seaweed forest, and I saw a shark tracking her. In an instant, she swam into a crack to escape, but the shark was faster.

The shark had taken a bite of one of her arms and was waiting for her. I wanted to save my friend, but in this environment, I could only observe. She managed to get deeper into the crack, but she was bleeding. After a while, the shark lost interest, and the octopus used the opportunity to get back to her den, without one of her arms. She was in serious danger because her arms function like the hands, legs, nose, and eyes of humans.

The next day, I was relieved to see that she had survived. She was weak, and her colors were not as bright. I checked on her every day, wondering if that day would be the last. It was emotionally painful to witness these things happening to her.

Recovery, Growth, and Sacrifice

A short while later, I saw that the wound had healed. To my amazement, a little arm started to grow back, and she started to become active again. I started to compare my life to life in the unforgiving sea. I thought of what was valuable in life. I began to spend more time with my family and friends, and I even started to dive with my young son. He became just as interested in her as I was. As the octopus's arm became more functional, I felt things in my life were improving too.

An octopus's average life is about a year, which ends after reproducing. One day, eight months after meeting her, I found her with another octopus. It was bittersweet knowing her final days were approaching even though she would bear young.

After mating, she didn't come out of her den. There would be no feeding or hunting. She was timing her final moments for the hatching of her eggs. After the eggs hatched, she died. A few months later, my son found a little octopus. We believe her story continues on.

I fell in love with an octopus and the amazing wildness she represented. I built a relationship with her and witnessed her life up to the final moments. I saw her from a perspective that I could not have had without this experience. She was smart, sensitive, and strong, often going through rough and tough days just like humans do. Eventually, she committed herself to protecting the birth of her young before she died. As a human being, I found something noble in that sacrifice. She was not simply an octopus; she was a part of this world just as I am a part of it now, and in that sense, we all have our own stories to tell.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 내가 어린 시절을 보냈던(spent) 곳. spending → spent (had + p.p. 과거완료)
det.analysis:
✅ ① spending → spent: had + p.p.(과거완료). had spending은 불가
❌ ② dense(빽빽한): 형용사로 seaweed forests 수식 정상
❌ ③ where: 관계부사, 장소 선행사 forests 수식 정상
❌ ④ octopus: 명사 정상
det.tip: had + p.p.(과거완료): had spent. 과거완료에서 현재분사(-ing) 사용 불가

questions.passage: Amazed at the cleverness of the octopus, I swam a little ①<u>closer</u>, but it disappeared. In fact, it had ②<u>lifting</u> a piece of seaweed, wrapped it around itself, and was ③<u>staring</u> at me out of a little gap. What an ④<u>extraordinary</u> creature!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 사실 해조류 한 조각을 들어올렸었다(lifted). lifting → lifted (had + p.p. 과거완료)
det.analysis:
✅ ② lifting → lifted: had + p.p.(과거완료). had lifting은 불가
❌ ① closer(비교급): 비교급 부사 정상
❌ ③ staring(진행형): was staring 정상
❌ ④ extraordinary(형용사): 감탄문 What an + 형용사 + 명사 정상
det.tip: had + p.p.(과거완료): had lifted. 과거완료에서 현재분사(-ing) 사용 불가

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 놀랍게도 → To my surprise. surprising → surprise (전치사 to + 소유격 my + 명사)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ surprising → surprise: 'To my surprise'에서 my 뒤에 명사 필요. surprising은 형용사
❌ ① scared(겁먹은): 과거분사/형용사 정상
❌ ② reached(뻗었다): 과거형 정상
❌ ④ top(꼭대기): 명사 정상
det.tip: To my surprise/amazement/delight = 놀랍게도/경탄하게도/기쁘게도. 소유격 뒤에 명사 필수!

questions.passage: The shark had taken a bite of one of her arms and was waiting for her. I wanted to save my friend, but in this environment, I could only ①<u>observe</u>. She ②<u>managed</u> to get deeper into the crack, but she was ③<u>bleeding</u>. She was in serious danger because her arms ④<u>functioned</u> like the hands, legs, nose, and eyes of humans.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 팔이 인간의 손, 다리, 코, 눈처럼 기능하기(function) 때문에. functioned → function (일반적 사실/현재 시제)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ functioned → function: 문어의 팔이 여러 기능을 한다는 일반적 사실(현재 시제). 과거형 부적절
❌ ① observe(관찰하다): could + 동사원형 정상
❌ ② managed(해냈다): 과거형 정상
❌ ③ bleeding(출혈 중인): was bleeding(과거 진행형) 정상
det.tip: 일반적 사실/불변의 진리 → 현재 시제. 문어의 팔 기능은 과거만의 사실이 아닌 일반적 사실

questions.passage: A short while later, I saw that the wound had healed. To my amazement, a little arm started to grow back, and she started to become active again. I started to compare my life to life in the __________ sea. I thought of what was valuable in life.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 가혹한(unforgiving) 바다에서의 삶과 내 삶을 비교하기 시작했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ unforgiving(가혹한): 상어에게 팔을 잃는 등 험한 바다 환경. 원문 일치
❌ ① forgiving(관대한): unforgiving의 반의어
❌ ② gentle(온화한): 바다의 가혹함과 반대
❌ ④ peaceful(평화로운): 상어 공격이 있는 환경과 맞지 않음
det.tip: unforgiving = 가혹한, 용서 없는. un- + forgiving. 자연의 잔인한 면을 표현

questions.passage: After ①<u>mating</u>, she didn't come out of her den. There would be no feeding or hunting. She was timing her final moments for the ②<u>hatching</u> of her eggs. After the eggs hatched, she died. A few months later, my son found a little octopus. We believe her story ③<u>ends</u> on. I fell in love with an octopus and the amazing ④<u>wildness</u> she represented.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 우리는 그녀의 이야기가 계속된다(continues)고 믿는다. ends(끝나다)는 continues(계속되다)의 반의어이므로 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ ends(끝나다) → continues(계속되다)가 원문. 아기 문어를 발견해서 이야기가 이어진다는 문맥
❌ ① mating(짝짓기): 원문 그대로
❌ ② hatching(부화): 원문 그대로
❌ ④ wildness(야생성): 원문 그대로
det.tip: continues on(계속되다) ↔ ends(끝나다). 새끼 문어의 발견 → 이야기가 끝나는 것이 아니라 이어짐

questions.passage: I returned to the Cape of Good Hope, South Africa, where I had spent my childhood, after over 20 years of movie-making. I went diving in the cold sea off the coast of the Cape, and it was among the dense seaweed forests where I met an octopus.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"화자는 어린 시절을 보냈던 희망봉에 20년 이상의 영화 제작 후 돌아왔다."

det.korean: 원문: I returned to the Cape of Good Hope after over 20 years of movie-making. 일치.
det.analysis:
✅ T: 원문 그대로 — 어린 시절을 보낸 곳, 20년 이상 영화 제작 후 복귀
❌ F: 원문과 정확히 일치하므로 F는 부적절
det.tip: Cape of Good Hope = 희망봉 (남아프리카 공화국). after over 20 years = 20년 이상 후

questions.passage: The shark had taken a bite of one of her arms and was waiting for her. I wanted to save my friend, but in this environment, I could only observe. She managed to get deeper into the crack, but she was bleeding.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"화자는 상어로부터 문어를 직접 구출했다."

det.korean: 원문: I wanted to save my friend, but I could only observe. 구출하지 못하고 관찰만 했다. 불일치.
det.analysis:
✅ F: '직접 구출했다'는 원문과 불일치. wanted to save이지만 could only observe
❌ T: 원문과 반대. 화자는 관찰만 할 수 있었음
det.tip: wanted to save ≠ actually saved. could only observe = 관찰만 할 수 있었다

questions.passage: An octopus's average life is about a year, which ends after reproducing. One day, eight months after meeting her, I found her with another octopus. It was bittersweet knowing her final days were approaching even though she would bear young.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 고르시오.

"문어의 평균 수명은 약 5년이며, 번식 후에도 계속 산다."

det.korean: 원문: average life is about a year, which ends after reproducing. 약 1년이며 번식 후 끝남. 5년+계속 산다는 불일치.
det.analysis:
✅ F: 원문은 약 1년(a year)이고 번식 후 끝남(ends). 5년+생존은 두 가지 모두 불일치
❌ T: 수명과 번식 후 생존 모두 원문과 다름
det.tip: about a year ≠ 5 years. ends after reproducing = 번식 후 끝남(죽음)

questions.passage: Amazed at the cleverness of the octopus, I swam a little closer, but it disappeared. In fact, it had lifted a piece of seaweed, wrapped it around itself, and was staring at me out of a little gap. What an extraordinary creature! I wondered what would happen if I kept watching it. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 어떤 드라마가 펼쳐질 것을 기대하며 기다렸다(waited).
det.analysis:
✅ ④ waited(기다렸다): 원문 일치. 카메라를 설치하고 정기 방문하며 기다림
❌ ① left immediately(즉시 떠났다): 계속 관찰하겠다는 의지와 반대
❌ ② called for help(도움을 요청했다): 문맥과 무관
❌ ③ gave up watching(관찰을 포기했다): 관찰을 계속하는 내용과 반대
det.tip: Expecting ~ I waited = 기대하며 기다렸다. 분사구문(Expecting)이 주절(waited)의 배경

questions.passage: I fell in love with an octopus and the amazing wildness she represented. I built a relationship with her and witnessed her life up to the final moments. I saw her from a perspective that I could not have had without this experience. She was smart, sensitive, and strong, often going through rough and tough days just like humans do. Eventually, she committed herself to protecting the birth of her young before she died. As a human being, I found something __________. She was not simply an octopus; she was a part of this world.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 인간으로서 그 희생에서 고귀한 것(noble in that sacrifice)을 발견했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① noble in that sacrifice: 새끼를 위해 헌신한 행위에서 고귀함 발견. 원문 일치
❌ ② frightening(무서운): 감동적 맥락에 부적합
❌ ③ boring(지루한): 감탄의 문맥과 반대
❌ ④ disappointing(실망스러운): 고귀함의 발견과 반대
det.tip: noble = 고귀한, 숭고한. sacrifice = 희생. committed herself to protecting → noble sacrifice

questions.passage: I saw a fish peacefully swimming near a heap of shells. Suddenly, an octopus sprang from the heap and grabbed the fish. Amazed at the cleverness of the octopus, I swam a little closer, but it disappeared. In fact, it had lifted a piece of seaweed, wrapped it around itself, and was staring at me out of a little gap.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 문어는 해조류로 자신을 위장하고 화자를 응시했다.
화자는 문어에게 더 가까이 다가가는 데 성공했다.

det.korean: 문어는 해조류를 들어올려 몸에 감싸고 작은 틈 사이로 화자를 응시했다(staring).
det.analysis:
✅ ② 해조류 위장+응시: lifted seaweed, wrapped it around itself, staring at me. 원문 일치
❌ ① 잡기 실패: grabbed the fish = 성공적으로 잡음
❌ ③ 더 가까이 성공: swam closer but it disappeared = 다가갔지만 사라짐
❌ ④ 조개 더미 속: 해조류로 위장한 것이지 조개 더미에 숨은 것이 아님
det.tip: wrapped ~ around itself = 몸에 감쌌다. staring at me = 나를 응시했다

questions.passage: The octopus became less scared as I visited more often. After about a month, it came near me. I put my hand out, and it reached out to me. After another week, it started to wave like a human friend saying, "Hi, I'm excited to see you." I kept still, and it covered my whole hand. Since I had to take a breath, I swam toward the surface. To my surprise, it rode on my hand all the way to the top.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 약 한 달 후 문어가 화자에게 다가왔다.
문어는 화자의 손 위에 올라타 수면까지 갔다.

det.korean: 원문: it covered my whole hand + rode on my hand all the way to the top. 손을 피하지 않고 손을 감싸고 수면까지 함께 감.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 손을 피해 도망: 원문은 손을 감싸고(covered) 수면까지 올라탐(rode). 도망이 아닌 친밀함
❌ ① 덜 무서워함: became less scared 원문 일치
❌ ② 한 달 후 다가옴: After about a month, it came near me 원문 일치
❌ ④ 수면까지 올라탐: rode on my hand all the way to the top 원문 일치
det.tip: covered my whole hand = 손 전체를 감쌌다. 이는 친밀함의 표현이지 도망이 아님

questions.passage: It sparked my curiosity in a way that I had not experienced before. Had I gained its trust? I started reading books about octopuses, but I wanted to learn more about this marvelous creature. The first thing I learned was that 'it' was a 'she.' Danger in the form of pyjama sharks, the area's biggest predators, came with little warning in the sea. The octopus was moving around near the edge of the seaweed forest, and I saw a shark tracking her. In an instant, she swam into a crack to escape, but the shark was more fast.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 찾아 바르게 고치시오.

det.korean: 상어가 더 빨랐다(faster). more fast → faster (1음절 형용사 비교급)
det.analysis:
✅ ① more fast → faster: fast는 1음절 형용사이므로 비교급은 faster. more fast는 비문
❌ ② tracking: saw + O + -ing (지각동사 + 현재분사) 정상
❌ ③ biggest: 최상급 (the area's biggest) 정상
❌ ④ gained: Had I gained (과거완료 의문문) 정상
det.tip: 1음절 형용사: fast → faster → fastest. more은 2음절 이상에 사용

questions.passage: After a while, the shark lost interest, and the octopus used the opportunity to get back to her den, without one of her arms. She was in serious danger because her arms function like the hands, legs, nose, and eyes of humans.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 찾아 쓰시오.

"상어가 관심을 잃자, 문어는 그 __________(을/를) 이용하여 팔 하나 없이 굴로 돌아갔다."

det.korean: 문어는 그 기회(opportunity)를 이용해 굴로 돌아갔다.
det.analysis: 원문 'used the opportunity'에서 opportunity를 찾아 쓰는 문제.
det.tip: opportunity = 기회. use the opportunity = 기회를 이용하다

questions.passage: I fell in love with an octopus and the amazing wildness she represented. I built a relationship with her and witnessed her life up to the final moments. She was smart, sensitive, and strong, often going through rough and tough days just like humans do.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 찾아 쓰시오.

"나는 문어와 관계를 쌓았고 마지막 순간까지 그녀의 삶을 __________(했다)."

det.korean: 마지막 순간까지 그녀의 삶을 목격했다(witnessed).
det.analysis: 원문 'witnessed her life up to the final moments'에서 witnessed를 찾아 쓰는 문제.
det.tip: witness = 목격하다, 증인이 되다. witnessed her life = 그녀의 삶을 지켜보았다

questions.passage: The octopus became less scared as I visited more often. After about a month, it came near me. I put my hand out, and it reached out to me. After another week, it started to wave like a human friend saying, "Hi, I'm excited to see you." I kept still, and it covered my whole hand. Since I had to take a breath, I swam toward the surface. __________, it rode on my hand all the way to the top.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 완성하시오. (대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능)

[ to / my / surprise ]

det.korean: 놀랍게도(To my surprise), 문어가 내 손 위에 올라타 꼭대기까지 갔다.
det.analysis: To my surprise = 놀랍게도. 전치사(to) + 소유격(my) + 명사(surprise) 어순.
det.tip: To my surprise = 놀랍게도. To one's + 감정명사 = ~하게도. 관용 표현

questions.passage: I started to compare my life to life in the unforgiving sea. I thought of what was valuable in life. I began to spend more time with my family and friends, and I even started to dive with my young son. He became just as interested in her as I was. As the octopus's arm became more functional, I felt things in my life were improving too.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 바다 다이빙은 위험하므로 혼자 하면 안 된다.
자연 속 경험이 삶의 가치관과 인간관계를 변화시킬 수 있다.
문어는 위험한 동물이므로 접근해서는 안 된다.
해양 생태계를 보호하기 위한 법률이 필요하다.

det.korean: 화자는 문어와의 경험을 통해 삶의 가치를 되새기고 가족과의 시간을 늘렸다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 자연 경험→삶 변화: compare my life + valuable in life + spend more time with family
❌ ① 위험 경고: 안전 이야기가 아님
❌ ③ 위험한 동물: 문어와 우정을 나누는 내용
❌ ④ 법률 필요: 환경보호 법률과 무관
det.tip: 핵심: I thought of what was valuable in life. 문어와의 교감이 삶의 성찰로 이어짐

questions.passage: I fell in love with an octopus and the amazing wildness she represented. I built a relationship with her and witnessed her life up to the final moments. She was smart, sensitive, and strong, often going through rough and tough days just like humans do. She was not simply an octopus; she was a part of this world just as I am a part of it now, and in that sense, we all have our own stories to tell.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 문어는 인간보다 뛰어난 지능을 가진 동물이다.
해양 생물을 애완동물로 키우는 것은 바람직하다.
자연 다큐멘터리 촬영에는 전문 장비가 필요하다.
모든 생물은 이 세계의 일부로서 각자의 이야기를 가지고 있다.

det.korean: 그녀는 단순한 문어가 아니라 이 세계의 일부이며, 우리 모두 각자의 이야기를 가지고 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 세계의 일부+각자의 이야기: a part of this world + our own stories to tell. 원문의 핵심 메시지
❌ ① 뛰어난 지능: 지능 비교가 아닌 존재적 연결
❌ ② 애완동물: 야생 관찰이지 사육이 아님
❌ ③ 전문 장비: 촬영 장비와 무관한 메시지
det.tip: 핵심: we all have our own stories to tell = 우리 모두 각자의 이야기가 있다. 인간과 자연의 연결

questions.passage: After mating, she didn't come out of her den. There would be no feeding or hunting. She was timing her final moments for the hatching of her eggs. After the eggs hatched, she died. A few months later, my son found a little octopus. We believe her story continues on.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말을 찾아 쓰시오.

"짝짓기 후, 문어는 알의 __________(을/를) 위해 마지막 순간을 맞추고 있었다."

det.korean: 알의 부화(hatching)를 위해 마지막 순간을 맞추고 있었다.
det.analysis: 원문 'timing her final moments for the hatching of her eggs'에서 hatching을 찾아 쓰는 문제.
det.tip: hatching = 부화. hatch(부화하다) → hatching(부화). timing for = ~을 위해 시간을 맞추다
